researcher_notes: 10 files, 6 unique documents (md5-deduplicated): P-series.pdf (3 pp), X-series.pdf (1 p), S-series-1.pdf == S-series-2.pdf (6 pp), RS-series-1.pdf == RS-series-1-2.pdf == RS-series-1-3.pdf == RS-series-3.pdf (6 pp), F12ML.pdf (1 p), F20MT.pdf (1 p). COMPANY ATTRIBUTION: none of the six documents prints a manufacturer name, logo or copyright line anywhere — they are bare spec cards headed only 'P-Series Robots P500R' etc. Attribution to Geek+ rests on the Tech Lead's standing decision (P/X/S/RS-series = Geek+) plus internal corroboration: the P-series page 2 mentions the '-EWE/-EWS version' and 'Popick', both Geek+ product names, and the RS-series model codes RS8-DA/RS11-DA match existing Geek+ DB rows exactly. DOCUMENT LAYOUT: every page uses the same four-block template (Product Dimensions / Battery & Power / Core Features & Performance / Safety & Environmental Adaptability) with a two-column bottom half; pdfplumber's plain text linearises this correctly here (labels and values stay paired), so no image rendering was needed. NOTE ON RS-series.pdf p.6: despite the filename it is headed 'P-Series Robots P40R', i.e. the RS-series PDF's last page documents a P-series robot. Extracted as P40R and mapped to the existing DB row 'Geek+ RoboShuttle P40'. 18 product entries below: 8 map to existing DB rows, 10 are new. The largest single finding is that the F12ML and F20MT lifting heights appear to be SWAPPED in the DB.

products.notes: NEW PRODUCT — the whole X-Series is absent from the DB. It is a genuinely distinct machine class for Geek+: a low-profile (125 mm tall) 1200 kg pallet mover with a 2 mm stop accuracy, five times tighter than anything else in the corpus. COLD-STORE CAPABILITY IS THE HEADLINE FINDING: the Cold Storage build is rated 0~-25 C. No other Geek+ product in this batch goes below -10 C, and a -25 C rating is a hard differentiator for frozen-goods tenders (operating_temp_min is COND_KO KO_IF_GT). Recorded -25 as operating_temp_min and 45 as operating_temp_max, i.e. the union across the two builds — FLAG FOR THE REVIEWER: no single unit covers both ends. The Cold Storage build's own upper bound is not published, and the Room Temperature build's lower bound is -10 C. If the import author prefers per-build rows, this should become two variants. NAVIGATION UNCERTAIN — the 'Navigation System' cell reads only 'Motor-driven', which is not a navigation method at all and looks like a template fill error by Geek+. 'Natural Feature (SLAM)' is recorded on the strength of the laser-based obstacle avoidance and the absence of any QR-code reference, but this is the weakest-sourced value in the group and should be verified before import. NOT MAPPED: weight 270 kg, obstacle 'Detection Distance 2.5 m', lift time 2.5 s, cycle life >=2000, run time ('Room Temperature: 1.2h charge for 8~10h use; Cold Storage: 2h charge for 6~8h use' — this IS a real charge time, 1.2 h = 72 min room-temp / 2 h = 120 min cold-store, but it is stated as a charge/use pair rather than a time-to-full, so charge_time was left null; a reviewer may reasonably record 120 as the conservative figure). FLOOR: an unusually detailed three-level spec — '2m distance: <=5mm height difference; 1m distance: <=8mm absolute height difference; Entire warehouse: <=20mm height difference; Ditch Width: <15mm'.

products.notes: CONFLICT 1 — lifting_height, and this is the largest single finding in the Geek+ group: the DB holds 120 mm for the F12ML and 3244 mm for the F20MT, but F12ML.pdf states 'Lifting Height 2300mm' and F20MT.pdf states 'Lifting Height 120mm'. The 120 belongs to the F20MT (a low-lift pallet mover) and has evidently been written onto the F12ML row. THE TWO ROWS LOOK SWAPPED, at least in part — note that the F20MT's stored 3244 mm matches NEITHER document, so this is not a clean transposition and both rows need re-sourcing rather than a simple exchange. lifting_height is a hard K.O. field, so a stacker currently stored as a 120 mm low-lifter fails every stacking tender. CONFLICT 2 — max_payload: DB 1400 kg; the sheet's derating table gives 1500 / 1200 / 1000 kg at 0-2 m / 2-2.5 m / 2.5-3 m. 1400 matches no cell. Recorded 1500 (the rated figure) per the convention used elsewhere in this pass, but note the honest answer at the truck's own full lift height of 2300 mm is 1200 kg — the payload-vs-lift-height derating gap flagged three times now this session (Toyota SAI125CB, Balyo VEENY, here). CONFLICT 3 — max_speed: DB 1.2 m/s; the sheet says 'Maximum speed of 1.5m/s'. Low stakes (SCORING field). INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY IN THE SOURCE: the derating table extends to 3 m but the stated lifting height is 2300 mm — the 2.5-3 m row describes a configuration this model cannot reach. Recorded as-is. SAFETY VERSION: a second build is offered with a 3.2 kW drive motor (vs 3.5 kW standard) and 'Lidar + Mechanical anti-collision' instead of a bumper strip. NOT MAPPED: fork dimensions 55x180x1200 mm and 'Spread: 560x620x680 mm' (three fork-spread positions — fork_spread was left null because the sheet does not say whether adjustment is manual or automatic), 'HMI Interface: Standard 10-inch display' and 'Smart Access: Swipe permission module' (AP0's onboard_ui is AMR-scope only, so an operator display on a Forklift AGV has no home — a scope gap), 'Motion Capabilities: Forward, backward, curved turns, and spin turns', lift speed 1.0/1.5 m/s, cycle life 1500, drive motor power. FLOOR: 'Flatness: Deviation <=5mm per 1m^2. Crossing Ability: Floor surface drop <=20mm recommended'.

products.notes: CONFLICT — lifting_height: the DB holds 3244 mm on this row; F20MT.pdf states 'Lifting Height 120mm'. See the F12ML entry: the two rows appear to have been mixed up, but not cleanly — 3244 mm matches NO figure in either document, so it must have come from a third source and both rows need re-sourcing. A 120 mm low-lifter stored as a 3.2 m stacker will wrongly PASS stacking tenders; the mirror-image error on the F12ML makes a real stacker fail them. DB max_payload 2000 CONFIRMED ('Up to 2000kg'). DB drive_type = 'Counterbalanced' NOT CONFIRMED and questioned: a 120 mm lift with a published fork spread (560/620/680 mm) is a pallet-mover geometry, not a counterbalanced truck; 'Pallet Mover' is proposed. Related: the DB also stores forks_free_floating = 1 and stacking_capability = 1 on this row, both of which sit oddly with a 120 mm lift. DB safety_standard = 'CE (EU models, verify)' is a non-conforming allowed value AND 'CE' is not in the safety_standard list at all (it belongs in Company-level certifications_generic); this sheet verifies CE and UKCA and adds PLd. Note the F20MT's lift SPEED is quoted in mm/s (35/40) while the F12ML's is quoted in m/s (1.0/1.5) — the F12ML figure is almost certainly also mm/s or is a different quantity; neither is storable, but it is a caution against reading Geek+ lift-speed rows at face value.

products.notes: NEW PRODUCT. The only S-Series model whose payload (100 kg) reaches the project's plausibility floor for a Mobile AMR, and by far the largest deck (750x1000 mm single package). Its charge ratio is also the best in the family: '10 minutes charge for 2-3 hours of work ... support user-defined scenario' vs 1.5 hours for the 20 kg models. OBSTACLE DETECTION differs from its siblings: 'Infrared sensor, support LiDAR' (i.e. infrared standard, lidar optional), where the S20 models all say 'Lidar obstacle detection' outright — a safety-relevant downgrade on the biggest robot in the family.
